title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: WA1 Person
tiers.description: All directors and senior management (including the Managing Director and Company Secretary), Key Management Personnel, all employees, and any other person the Board designates in writing, plus a company or trust they control. For clause 3 (Blackout Periods/notifications) only, also extends to spouse, child, close relative, or a person financially dependent on or acting in concert with them.

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: WA1 may impose, without notice and in its sole and absolute discretion, additional restrictions on trading by any or all WA1 Persons (or other staff), even outside a mandated Blackout Period. Confidential: any restriction communicated under clause 3.2 must be kept strictly confidential.

short_term.evidence: Under no circumstances should WA1 Persons engage in short-term or speculative trading in WA1 securities. This prohibition includes short term direct dealing in WA1 securities as well as transactions in the derivative markets, involving exchange traded options, share warrants, contracts for difference, and other similar instruments, which are short term or speculative.

exemption_authority: The Authorising Officer for the relevant tier (Managing Director for the Chair; Chair of the Board for other directors/Company Secretary/KMP; Company Secretary or Managing Director for other WA1 Persons) has absolute discretion under clause 3.4 to approve dealing in exceptional circumstances (severe financial hardship or a court order, without limitation) during a Blackout Period or otherwise-prohibited dealing, except where it would breach insider trading laws. The decision is final and binding, needs no reasons, and must be kept strictly confidential by the WA1 Person.

bespoke_clauses.topic: secured financing carve-out for vested shares
bespoke_clauses.clause: Unless clause 4.3(a) applies, WA1 Persons may, directly or indirectly, grant security (whether by charge, mortgage, pledge or otherwise) over any of WA1's securities, to secure any obligation of that WA1 Person or any third party or enter into any margin lending arrangements involving WA1 securities, with consent provided under clause 3.3.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike many peer policies, WA1 expressly permits the loan leg of a funded collar secured on vested, unrestricted shares, subject only to ordinary Authorising Officer consent, not an exceptional-circumstances gate.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The entering into of all types of "protection arrangements" for any WA1 securities (or WA1 products in the derivatives markets): is prohibited at any time in respect of any WA1 securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock; and otherwise, requires consent under clause 3.3.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar's put and call fall within 'protection arrangements'; over vested, unrestricted shares they need only ordinary clause 3.3 consent (the same regime as for dealing outside a Blackout Period), not the narrower 'exceptional circumstances' standard used elsewhere in the policy for Blackout Period trading.

bespoke_clauses.clause: prior to dealing in WA1 securities outside a Blackout Period or where clause 4 requires the person to obtain a consent under clause 3.3, notify the relevant person ... and obtain consent from the Authorising Officer.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Both the derivative/hedging consent and the secured-financing consent for vested shares are gated by the routine notify-and-consent process, materially easier to obtain than a hardship/court-order threshold.

bespoke_clauses.clause: a disposal of WA1 securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights under a loan or security agreement
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank's enforcement sale on default is excluded from Blackout Period and other policy restrictions, giving a clean enforcement path.

bespoke_clauses.clause: WA1 may impose, without notice and in its sole and absolute discretion, additional restrictions on trading ... Any restriction communicated ... must be kept strictly confidential.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An undisclosed ad-hoc restriction can block collar entry, unwind or settlement at any time without the executive being able to explain the delay to the bank.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If an WA1 Person comes into possession of Inside Information after receiving a clearance to trade, they must not trade despite having received the clearance.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A cleared collar transaction can become unexecutable if inside information arises before signing, even after consent is granted.

summary: A funded collar over vested, unrestricted WA1 shares is achievable and comparatively favourable: clause 4.3(b) expressly permits granting security over such shares and entering into margin lending arrangements with ordinary Authorising Officer consent under clause 3.3, so the loan leg is not banned outright. The put and call together are a 'protection arrangement' under clause 4.2, banned absolutely over unvested or holding-locked shares but, over vested unrestricted shares, permitted with the same ordinary clause 3.3 consent (not the narrower 'exceptional circumstances' standard reserved for Blackout Period overrides). A secured lender's enforcement sale on default is excluded from Blackout Period and other restrictions, giving the bank a workable path. Short-term or speculative trading (including via CFDs and exchange-traded options) is banned outright under clause 4.1 with no clearance route, so collar tenor should avoid that characterisation, and any consent lapses if inside information arises before execution or can be withdrawn if circumstances change. Overall, subject to ordinary consent and staying outside Blackout Periods, both legs of the structure are workable for vested, unrestricted shares.
